examples.solution_text:
By the null factor law, at least one factor is zero.
$\begin{aligned}x-7&=0\text{ or }x+4=0\\x&=7\text{ or }x=-4\end{aligned}$

Product $=-24$, sum $=2$. The pair is $6$ and $-4$.
$\begin{aligned}(x+6)(x-4)&=0\\x+6&=0\text{ or }x-4=0\\x&=-6\text{ or }x=4\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Solve $x^{2}-14x+49=0$ and explain why it has only one solution.
examples.solution_text:
Product $=49$, sum $=-14$. The pair is $-7$ and $-7$.
$\begin{aligned}(x-7)^{2}&=0\\x-7&=0\\x&=7\end{aligned}$
Both factors are the same, so there is only one solution.

Subtract $11x$ from both sides before factorising.
$x^{2}-11x+28=0$
Product $=28$, sum $=-11$. The pair is $-4$ and $-7$.
$\begin{aligned}(x-4)(x-7)&=0\\x-4&=0\text{ or }x-7=0\\x&=4\text{ or }x=7\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Solve $3x^{2}+12x-36=0$ by first taking out the common factor.
examples.solution_text:
$3(x^{2}+4x-12)=0$
Product $=-12$, sum $=4$. The pair is $6$ and $-2$.
$3(x+6)(x-2)=0$
The factor $3$ cannot be zero. By the null factor law:
$\begin{aligned}x+6&=0\text{ or }x-2=0\\x&=-6\text{ or }x=2\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: A student solves $(x-2)(x+3)=14$ by writing $x-2=14$ or $x+3=14$. Explain the mistake and solve correctly.
examples.solution_text:
The null factor law requires a product of zero. Expand and subtract $14$ first.
$\begin{aligned}x^{2}+x-6&=14\\x^{2}+x-20&=0\end{aligned}$
Product $=-20$, sum $=1$. The pair is $5$ and $-4$.
$\begin{aligned}(x+5)(x-4)&=0\\x+5&=0\text{ or }x-4=0\\x&=-5\text{ or }x=4\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: The temperature in a room is $t^{2}-7t+12$ degrees Celsius, where $t$ is the number of hours after $8$ am. Find the times when the temperature is $0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
examples.solution_text:
$t^{2}-7t+12=0$
Product $=12$, sum $=-7$. The pair is $-3$ and $-4$.
$\begin{aligned}(t-3)(t-4)&=0\\t-3&=0\text{ or }t-4=0\\t&=3\text{ or }t=4\end{aligned}$
The temperature is $0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ at $11$ am and $12$ noon.

Expand and collect all terms on the left.
$\begin{aligned}x^{2}+5x&=3x+18-x\\x^{2}+5x&=2x+18\\x^{2}+3x-18&=0\end{aligned}$
Product $=-18$, sum $=3$. The pair is $6$ and $-3$.
$\begin{aligned}(x+6)(x-3)&=0\\x+6&=0\text{ or }x-3=0\\x&=-6\text{ or }x=3\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: The square of a number is $9$ times the same number. Find every possible value of the number.
examples.solution_text:
Let the number be $x$.
$\begin{aligned}x^{2}&=9x\\x^{2}-9x&=0\\x(x-9)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }x-9=0\\x&=0\text{ or }x=9\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: The zero product gives x−7=0 or x+4=0, hence x=7 or x=−4.
6×(−4)=−24 and 6+(−4)=2, so the factorisation is (x+6)(x−4)=0 and the solutions are −6 and 4.
(−7)×(−7)=49 and −7−7=−14. Thus (x−7)²=0 gives the single distinct solution x=7.
Subtracting 11x gives x²−11x+28=0. The constants −4 and −7 have product 28 and sum −11, giving x=4 or x=7.
Extracting 3 gives 3(x²+4x−12)=0=3(x+6)(x−2). Since 3 is nonzero, x=−6 or x=2.
Expanding gives x²+x−6=14, hence x²+x−20=0=(x+5)(x−4). The solutions −5 and 4 each give the original product 14. The null factor law cannot be applied directly to that nonzero product.
Zero temperature requires t²−7t+12=(t−3)(t−4)=0, so t=3 or 4 hours after 8 am: 11 am and 12 noon.
Expansion gives x²+5x=2x+18, hence x²+3x−18=(x+6)(x−3)=0. The solutions are x=−6 and x=3.
The verbal condition gives x²=9x. Rearranging and extracting x gives x(x−9)=0, retaining both solutions x=0 and x=9.
